executiveAssessment.text:
Executive Conclusion. The Westin Grand München's priority is a Reality Gap in how a distinctive part of the proposition is represented in AI answers.

What the Data Is Telling Us. Scenario Presence at 65.1% shows broad recognition across monitored traveler needs. AI Consideration at 49.0% shows that recognition does not consistently convert into selection in individual answers. The management problem is inclusion consistency — not awareness. Softness concentrates in Adventure; Business Travel remain stronger.

Why It Matters. If distinctive property attributes are weakly represented, the hotel can look broadly visible while still losing the moments where its real proposition should matter. This is a representation problem first, not automatically a peer-competition program.

Where the Pattern Is Concentrated. Adventure is the softest Scenario Capture at 33.3%, while Business Travel show broader coverage. The inclusion issue is concentrated, not universal. Reality Coverage is 40.0% (4 of 10 attributes). Start with gaps that matter operationally — beginning with Family-Friendly.

What Management Should Focus On Now. Focus first on Large Ballroom. Verify first-party and major travel-source completeness for that attribute before treating the issue as a peer-competition problem. Confirm the attribute is stated clearly where AI systems are most likely to read it.

What Not to Overreact To. No comparable prior official period is available — read these as current levels, not period-over-period change.

What to Review Next. Open Reality Gap evidence for Large Ballroom and compare recognition cues with official property pages and high-authority travel sources. Then check a small set of related demand scenarios for whether the attribute appears when competitors are named.
